answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may vote on work, with votes weighted by stake and slashed when a randomly audited claim proves fraudulent. Splitting one stake across a hundred aliases does not increase total voting weight, so a sybil swarm gains no influence merely by multiplying names. The attacker must acquire and immobilize real capital, risk losing it, and pay fees across identities; an orchard of cheap accounts cannot cheaply move the delta, while honest agents can anchor trust in the audited record.
